texts: mixed: the group-level record is right (who lit what, at sundown on day 630 of Year 2), but because the subject is a bare plural and the object a definite plural, the parse also lays down a per-Keeper rule that hands the whole lantern group to each Keeper, so it reads as 'each Keeper lit every lantern' — more than the sentence claims. Rewrite as "On day 630 of Year 2, the Keepers together lit the lanterns of the East Row at sundown.": 'together' marks the lighting as joint work, so only the single group event is recorded.

good. the group event and the per-lantern rule both come out faithful here, because the object is a kind rather than a specific set — 'each lantern burned mire-essence' is exactly what the sentence says.
good. same shape as the previous sentence and equally faithful: the lanterns as a group and each lantern separately produce mist-light.
good. the attracting event, the mist-light as what does the attracting, and the nightmoths drawn to it are all covered.
good. the crowd is recorded as one thing whose members are nightmoths, and 'gathered' stays collective — no false claim that each moth gathered on its own.
good. the four-cat group, its count of four, the cliff-spires they came from and the per-cat descent all come through.
good. the hunt is recorded both for the four cats as a group and for each cat, and the crowd hunted is correctly the same crowd that gathered.
good. shrinking is kept as something that happened to the crowd as a whole, which is right — nothing claims individual moths shrank.
good. this becomes a rule that actually fires: any nightmoth that survived that particular hunt gets its own flight to the Hollows, and the 'each' is recorded alongside.
good. the molting is tied to the hunt by 'during' and handed to each of the four cats.

mixed: the falling, the feathers and the base of the cliff are all recorded, but nothing connects these feathers to the molting in the previous sentence — a bare 'Feathers' reads as a fresh, unrelated set of feathers. If they are the molted ones, rewrite as "Feathers from the four sky-cats fell to the base of the cliff.", which keeps the origin explicit and links back to the cats already introduced.

mixed: two things go wrong at once — 'Nightmoths' bare mints a second, unrelated moth set rather than the crowd already at the East Row, and the per-moth rule hands the whole thread bundle to each moth ('every moth left every thread'). Rewrite as "The nightmoth crowd left silken threads on the lanterns of the East Row.": the definite phrase points back at the crowd, and because 'crowd' is singular the predication stays on the crowd as a unit.

mixed: the collecting, the threads, the lanterns, dawn and the date are all covered, but the per-Keeper rule again gives the whole bundle of threads to each Keeper, and 'Keepers' bare introduces a third, unrelated Keeper set rather than the ones who lit the lanterns. Rewrite as "The Keepers together collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 631 of Year 2.": 'the Keepers' points back at the earlier group and 'together' keeps the collecting a single joint act.
good. Hesper, the threads, the sea-water as the medium, the three cauldrons and the date are all recorded, and boiling correctly registers as something that changes the threads.
